questions.question: The height of a cylinder is 45 cm. If circumference of its base is 132 cm, then what is the curved surface of this cylinder ? (use π = 22/7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of a cylinder = Base Circumference × Height

Given Circumference = 132 cm and Height = 45 cm

CSA = 132 × 45

CSA = 132 × (50 − 5) = 6600 − 660 = 5940 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 5940 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height (h) = 45 cm

Circumference of base (2πr) = 132 cm

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cylinder = 2 × π × r × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/16d1e6ab67c082221de5b1b402ecbe6fd456eddce8286635fd7df31477e3a541.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Base Circumference = 2 × π × r = 132 cm

⇒ Curved Surface Area = (2 × π × r) × h

⇒ CSA = 132 × 45

⇒ CSA = 5940 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 5940 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

TSA includes the curved surface and the areas of the two circular bases: TSA = 2πr(r + h).

Volume of Cylinder

The space occupied by the cylinder is given by Volume = Base Area × Height = πr²h.

Base Radius Calculation

If required, the radius (r) can be found from circumference: r = Circumference ÷ 2π. For 132 cm, r = (132 × 7) ÷ (2 × 22) = 21 cm.</p

questions.question: How many composite numbers are there from 53 to 97 ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total integers from 53 to 97 = 97 − 53 + 1 = 45.

List primes in the range: 53, 59, 61, 67, 71, 73, 79, 83, 89, 97 (Total 10 primes).

Composite numbers = Total numbers − Prime numbers.

Composite numbers = 45 − 10 = 35.

**∴ The correct answer is 35.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Range of numbers: 53 to 97 (inclusive).

**Formula Used:**

Total numbers in range [a, b] = (b − a) + 1

Composite numbers = Total numbers − Prime numbers (for n > 1)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4528d8d78df34309ff9db556970d605872a76265bc27d950a66583533a7fe19a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total integers between 53 and 97 = 97 − 53 + 1 = 45.

⇒ Prime numbers between 53 and 97 are: 53, 59, 61, 67, 71, 73, 79, 83, 89, 97.

⇒ Count of prime numbers = 10.

⇒ Count of composite numbers = 45 − 10 = 35.

**∴ The correct answer is 35.**

**__Additional Information__**

Composite Numbers

A composite number is a positive integer greater than 1 that has at least one divisor other than 1 and itself.

Prime Numbers

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. There are 25 prime numbers between 1 and 100.

Special Cases

The number 1 is neither prime nor composite. The number 2 is the smallest prime number and the only even prime number.</p

questions.question:
A alone can do a work in 11 days. B alone can do the same work in 22 days. C alone can do the same work in 33 days.

They work in the following manner :

Day 1: A and B work.

Day 2: B and C work.

Day 3: C and A work.

Day 4: A and B work. And so on.

In how many days will the work be completed ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(11, 22, 33) = 66 units.

Efficiencies: A = 6, B = 3, C = 2 units/day.

Work in 1 cycle (3 days): (A+B) + (B+C) + (C+A) = (6+3) + (3+2) + (2+6) = 22 units.

Total cycles needed = Total Work ÷ Work per cycle = 66 ÷ 22 = 3 cycles.

Total days = 3 cycles × 3 days/cycle = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Time taken by A = 11 days

Time taken by B = 22 days

Time taken by C = 33 days

Formula used: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Calculations:

⇒ Day 1 Work (A + B) = 6 + 3 = 9 units

⇒ Day 2 Work (B + C) = 3 + 2 = 5 units

⇒ Day 3 Work (C + A) = 2 + 6 = 8 units

⇒ Total work done in 3 days (1 cycle) = 9 + 5 + 8 = 22 units

⇒ Total work to be completed = 66 units

⇒ Number of cycles = 66 ÷ 22 = 3 cycles

⇒ Total time = 3 × 3 = 9 days

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternate Day Work

In problems where work is done on alternate days or in a specific cyclic pattern, calculate the total work done in one complete cycle first and then divide the total work by the cycle sum.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each individual, which is proportional to their Efficiency × Time.

Pipes and Cisterns

This concept is identical to Time and Work, where an outlet pipe has negative efficiency (emptying work) and an inlet pipe has positive efficiency (filling work).</p
